Sigil Encoding

Encoding Pathfinder Second Edition spells

Sigil generates drawings that encode nine mechanical attributes of a Pathfinder Second Edition spell and its source / variant ID. The annotated example below shows the complete encoding before rank-based display filtering.

Representing every attribute as vertex-to-vertex connections (chords) produced crowded drawings. The notation therefore separates five primary attributes into chord families and four secondary attributes into vertex-centered orbits. A third layer stores the ID because different spells can share the same mechanical attributes.

The layers in Figure 1 correspond to the editor's Notation panels:

Layer On the canvas Encodes
1 - Vertices Chords between numbered points Five primary attributes
2 - Orbits An arc or ring around a point Four secondary attributes
3 - Spell fingerprint Ordered marks and gaps Source / variant ID

Sigil is an independent adaptation of The Spell Writing Guide and SpellWriting, by The Gorilla of Destiny. Vertex-centered orbits, the fingerprint, and rank-based filtering are Sigil extensions. This reference does not require the original guide.

Spell data and preprocessing

The bundled catalogue, data/spell.json, comes from fyjham-ts/Pathfinder-2E-Spell-DB. Removing one duplicate record each for Light, Invisibility, and Clairvoyance reduced the original 1,403 records to 1,400. Each record retains its description, source book and page, and nethysUrl linking to Archives of Nethys.

On import, the parser normalizes raw fields into rank, exact tradition combinations, damage, area, range, casting time, duration, Primary Trait, and casting traits. Descriptions and publication references remain separate from the encoded categories.

The parser uses the first nonempty identifier from variant, sourceId, uuid, _id, id, slug, or an object key. If none is available, it falls back to the Archives of Nethys page ID, for example aon-1662, or generates a content-based ID if that is also missing. IDs are shortened and disambiguated as needed.

From fields to bits

For \(m\) primary attributes, the implementation selects the vertex count as

\[ n = \operatorname{nextPrime}(2m+1) = 11. \tag{1}\]

Here \(m = 5\), and nextPrime selects the smallest prime at least as large as \(2m+1\). At eleven vertices, steps 1 through 5 define distinct undirected chord families; steps 6 through 10 repeat them in reverse. No vertex pair therefore belongs to two attribute families. A prime vertex count also ensures that all nonconstant binary necklaces have the same number of distinct rotations.

Both mechanical layers use eleven-bit binary words indexed from 0 to 10, left to right. A set bit activates its vertex. The editor's optional number labels use 01 to 11 for the same positions, as illustrated in Figure 1. The value none bypasses the dictionary and encodes as the all-zero word.

The dictionary contains one representative per binary necklace, chosen as its lexicographically smallest rotation. The all-zero and all-one words are excluded. Since 11 is prime, each remaining necklace has 11 distinct rotations, giving

\[ N = \frac{2^{11}-2}{11} = 186. \tag{2}\]

For the eleven-vertex layout, representatives with Hamming weight \(w\) are sorted by increasing distance \(\lvert w-4\rvert\), with lexicographic tie-breaking. This heuristic favors four active bits to reduce visual clutter. For an option at zero-based index \(q\) in its attribute's ordered list, excluding none, the encoder selects dictionary entry \(q\) and rotates it left by

\[ r(q) = (7q+3)\bmod 11. \tag{3}\]

The simplified rotation in Equation 3 applies to the shipped eleven-vertex layout. Reproduction requires the same dictionary and option ordering, including Range choices appended from a catalogue. A tradition subset such as Arcane+Primal occupies one option.

Calculate the layers

Layer 1 - Vertices

Each primary attribute is assigned a chord step \(k\):

Attribute Step \(k\)
Rank 1
Tradition 2
Range 3
Duration 4
Primary Trait 5

Each active bit at vertex index \(i\) contributes the undirected chord

\[ \{i,\ (i+k)\bmod 11\}. \tag{4}\]

With the vertex count from Equation 1, the five families in Equation 4 partition all \(11 \cdot 10 / 2 = 55\) vertex pairs without overlap.

Layer 2 - Orbits

Let \(b_{a,i}\) denote attribute \(a\)'s bit at vertex \(i\). The four secondary attributes determine an orbit value \(U_i\) and sweep angle \(\theta_i\):

\[ \begin{aligned} U_i &= b_{\text{Damage},i} + 2b_{\text{Area},i} + 4b_{\text{Casting time},i} + 8b_{\text{Casting traits},i},\\ \theta_i &= \frac{360^\circ U_i}{15} = 24^\circ U_i. \end{aligned} \tag{5}\]

The power-of-two weights in Equation 5 distinguish all sixteen bit combinations. \(U_i = 0\) produces no orbit, \(1 \leq U_i \leq 14\) a partial arc, and \(U_i = 15\) a complete 360-degree circle. A complete circle occurs only when all four secondary bits are active at the same vertex.

Layer 3 - Spell fingerprint

The fingerprint payload is ["spell-id", variant] serialized as compact JSON, with the source / variant ID represented as a string, or the empty string if absent. Its UTF-8 bytes are prefixed by their count as an unsigned 16-bit integer. The header and payload bytes are written most significant bit first. For a payload of \(B\) bytes, the fingerprint length in bits is

\[ L = 16 + 8B,\qquad B \leq 192. \tag{6}\]

The 192-byte limit in Equation 6 is an implementation constraint intended to keep the fingerprint legible. It applies to the complete payload, not the ID alone. Each bit occupies a marker slot: 1 is marked and 0 remains unmarked. This layer stores the ID rather than a name or mechanics hash; reusing an ID produces the same fingerprint.

What the editor displays

The editor enables Filter details by rank by default. Applied after complete encoding and before rendering, it retains all \(R\) Rank chords and the complete fingerprint. The remaining chords and whole orbits form an optional pool of size \(M\). For display fraction \(f\), the visible mechanical count is

\[ V = R + \lceil fM\rceil. \tag{7}\]

In Equation 7, \(f\) is 20% for cantrips, 40% for ranks 1-3, 60% for 4-6, 80% for 7-8, and 100% for 9-10. Disabling the filter sets \(f = 1\), as in Figure 1. Optional elements are selected in round-robin order from Tradition, Orbits (sorted by vertex), Range, Duration, and Primary Trait, skipping exhausted pools. Orbits are selected intact; filtering never changes their sweep angles.

The renderer fits the complete geometry to the chosen contour before drawing the visible subset. Curvature, orbit size, colors, ink treatment, and marker shape affect appearance rather than encoded data. Hidden elements remain in the complete representation, but a filtered or styled image is not guaranteed to support lossless decoding.

Worked example

The fictional spell in Figure 1 uses the following attribute values. Its attribute names match the editor's Notation controls; none indicates no selected value. The results trace Acid through the dictionary and rotation, then summarize the complete encoding and cantrip-filtered view. Arrays are in vertex order.

Attribute Value
Spell rank cantrip
Tradition Arcane
Range category Self
Duration Instant
Primary trait Healing
Damage type Acid
Area shape none
Casting time 1 action
Casting traits none
Source / variant ID demo-1
Full fingerprint bit sequence

The sequence encodes ["spell-id","demo-1"]. The first line is the length header; subsequent lines contain payload bytes. Whitespace is not encoded.

0000000000010101
01011011 00100010 01110011
01110000 01100101 01101100
01101100 00101101 01101001
01100100 00100010 00101100
00100010 01100100 01100101
01101101 01101111 00101101
00110001 00100010 01011101
Property Result
Option index (Acid) 0
Dictionary entry "00000001111"
Left rotation 3
Non-none bits "00001111000"
None bits "00000000000"
Active vertices [4, 5, 6, 7]
Rank chords 4
Other chords 16
Orbits 4
Orbit units [5, 5, 5, 5]
Orbit sweeps (degrees) [120, 120, 120, 120]
Fingerprint payload bytes 21
Fingerprint bits 184
Optional elements 20
Optional elements shown 4
Visible mechanical elements 8
Total mechanical elements 24

Follow the calculation

  1. Acid is the first non-none Damage option, so \(q = 0\). Dictionary entry 0 is 00000001111. Using Equation 3 gives \(r(0) = 3\), producing 00001111000 and active vertex indices 4, 5, 6, 7. Every other non-none selection in this example also has index 0 and receives the same word.
  2. Applying Equation 4 at each active vertex index produces one chord per primary attribute. Rank has \(k = 1\), yielding 4 to 5, 5 to 6, 6 to 7, and 7 to 8. The four other families contribute sixteen further chords.
  3. Damage and Casting time contribute 1 and 4 at each active vertex; Area and Casting traits contribute zero. By Equation 5, each of the four orbits has \(U_i = 1 + 4 = 5\) and a sweep of \(5 \cdot 24 = 120\) degrees.
  4. With \(R = 4\), \(M = 16 + 4 = 20\), and cantrip display fraction \(f = 0.2\), Equation 7 gives \(V = 4 + \lceil 0.2 \cdot 20\rceil = 8\) visible mechanical elements out of 24. The 21-byte fingerprint payload gives \(L = 16 + 8 \cdot 21 = 184\) fingerprint bits by Equation 6, unaffected by filtering.

Select optimal attributes for Pathfinder spells

Seven attributes were selected manually, and two were selected through an exhaustive search. Rank, Tradition, Damage, Area, Range, Casting time, and Duration were chosen as mechanics worth representing. The search then identified the two additional attributes that distinguished the most spells when combined with those seven.

Using the original 1,403 records, the search tested all 21 pairs from spell type, defense, targets, rarity, Primary Trait, Casting traits, and heightening. For comparison, it also tested 2,002 unrestricted nine-of-fourteen combinations. The search maximizes the number of uniquely identified spells, then minimizes matching pairs, then maximizes distinct combinations. Remaining ties are resolved lexicographically by the ordered list of attribute identifiers.

Comparison uses only the selected categorical values, excluding name, edition, ID, and description:

  • The "Spells with a unique combination" column counts spells whose attribute combination appears exactly once in the analysed catalogue.
  • The "Combinations found" column counts the different attribute combinations observed in the catalogue, including shared ones, rather than the theoretical number of possible combinations.
  • The "Pairs sharing a combination" column counts pairs of spells with identical attribute combinations, counting each pair once.

Three spells sharing one combination contribute one observed combination and three matching pairs, but no uniquely identified spells. Uniqueness is measured within this catalogue, not guaranteed for future or custom spells.

Attributes Spells with a unique combination Combinations found Pairs sharing a combination
Required seven 1,098 1,222 307
Seven + heightening 1,215 1,294 170
Seven + Primary Trait + Casting traits (selected) 1,288 1,338 87
Seven + Casting traits + heightening 1,287 1,340 76
Best unrestricted nine 1,332 1,362 55
All fourteen 1,352 1,374 38

Adding Primary Trait and Casting traits uniquely identifies 91.8% of spells in this dataset. Casting traits plus heightening produces fewer matching pairs but identifies one fewer spell uniquely. The unrestricted nine-attribute optimum omits required Damage, Area, and Range and is therefore ineligible. Even all fourteen attributes leave mechanically indistinguishable records, motivating the separate ID fingerprint.

Verification

npm run test:math reads the example's input table, results, and fingerprint directly from this document and checks them against the implementation. It also checks all sixteen orbit masks. The tests do not repeat the attribute selection search. Use npm run optimize, optionally with -- /path/to/spell.json, to run the search on a catalogue. After npm run compile, machine-readable results are available through node src/tools/optimize-attributes.js --json.
